title: Biological Sample Lysis and Extraction Using Covaris LE220+ for LC-MS
author: ronan o'cualain

If finished, logout of the Sonolab software and return the rack to the side of the LE220+ for the next user. IMPORTANT: The Sonolab software should be always left ON, as by shutting it down, the default settings are triggered and the day to day maintenance settings are lost. If the software needs to be re-booted, contact a member of the facility. Do not shut down the software! Notes: Treatments are defined by the following parameters: (For an in-depth explanation of these parameters, go to covaris.com) Treatment time. Cycles per Burst – the number of acoustic oscillations contained in each burst. The illustration below shows five cycles in each burst. Duty Factor – the percentage of active burst time in the acoustic treatment. The illustration shows a Duty Factor of 20%. Peak Incident Power – the power, in Watts, being emitted from the transducer during each burst. Average Incident Power - Peak Incident Power multiplied by the Duty Factor. (For an in-depth explanation of these parameters, go to covaris.com)

steps.title: Prepare working lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Dilute the 2× S‑Trap lysis buffer (10 % SDS) to a 5 % SDS, 50 mM TEAB pH 7.5 working stock by adding 500 µL of the 2× stock to 500 µL LC‑MS grade water using a 1 mL pipette; if samples contain many disulfide bonds, add DTT to a final concentration of 5 mM (prepare DTT as described in the reduction‑alkylation section).

steps.title: Add buffer to samples
steps.instruction: Dispense the 5 % SDS, 50 mM TEAB buffer into the sample tubes, avoiding any freezing after buffer addition.

substeps.instruction: For 520045 tubes, add approximately 50 µL–130 µL of buffer (do not use 100 µL, as excessive headspace impairs performance).
For 520185 tubes, add up to 500 µL of buffer, adjusting volume to the amount of sample present.

steps.title: Load tubes into Covaris rack
steps.instruction: Place the Covaris tubes (containing the lysed samples) into the stainless‑steel rack, ensuring that every position in a row is filled (rows of 4 or 8 with no gaps) and using spare tubes beside the machine if needed.

steps.title: Secure rack and keep on ice
steps.instruction: Clamp the rack lid finger‑tight, then keep the rack on ice until you are ready to start the ultrasonication.

steps.title: Prepare LE220+ instrument
steps.instruction: Log onto the LE220+ focused ultrasonicator and verify that the “Run” box in the top‑right corner is green; if it is red or shows an X next to temperature, wait until the system reaches the set temperature (default 10 °C, or 6 °C if your method specifies).

substeps.instruction: If needed, select an alternative method from the drop‑down menu on the HOME tab (top left).
Click “Edit” to specify which rows of the plate to process; for two rows, select them via the left‑hand process panel and confirm on the right‑hand display.
Save the selection and return to the main menu; the Run button will become active only after a method is selected and all conditions (e.g., temperature) are met.

steps.title: Load plate into instrument
steps.instruction: Click the “Motion Control” box, then “Load” to move the plate holder to the front of the LE220+; open the door by pressing the green lock button while gently pulling the safety enclosure handle; load the plate with the orientation specified in the method.

steps.title: Run sonication program
steps.instruction: When the “Run” button turns green, click it to start the selected method; monitor the flashing row graphic and the displayed average incident power and temperature data until the method completes.

steps.title: Retrieve and store lysate
steps.instruction: After the “Method Complete” message appears, click OK, press the green door‑lock button, open the safety enclosure, remove the plate and place it on ice; label 0.5 mL or 1.5 mL tubes for each 520045 or 520185 tube processed, transfer the lysed extract into the labeled tubes, and either freeze the samples for storage or proceed to reduction and alkylation.
